title: Fomo Kernel Agent-Supplied Price Feed
description: Closing prices, an FX rate, or both, transcribed from a recognized market-data source when the host cannot retrieve them itself. Declared facts only: the agent never computes a return, a weight, or a P&L number. Every close and history entry is a RAW market observation as printed on its own session date; never send a split-adjusted price. The engine rebases each observation onto the split basis of the share count it will be multiplied by, using that row's date against the declared splits. `prices` and `fx` are each optional (#642) -- a host that can read one public FX rate but not every instrument's close may supply `fx` alone, which is what makes a book refused only for a missing rate on a currency its account aggregate spans (#612, and #649 for a currency that only a cash-flow row carries) repairable without fabricating closes nobody asked for -- but the envelope must declare at least one of the two; see `anyOf` below.

as_of.description: Non-future end-of-day date this feed represents; no row may be dated after it.

source.description: Feed-level provenance, named on the card. Use the market-data source, not a search engine.

prices.description: One row per priced instrument. Optional when `fx` is supplied and non-empty (#642): omit it entirely, or send an empty list, for a rate-only repair. See the top-level `anyOf` -- an envelope needs at least one of `prices` or `fx`.

ticker.description: The complete engine symbol, matching the trade rows (for example NVDA, 2330.TW, ^TWII).

close.description: Raw closing price as printed on `date`, in the instrument's own trading currency. Do not adjust it for a split yourself: state the observation and declare the split in `splits`, and the engine rebases it onto the share count's basis.

date.description: Session date of this close, and therefore the split basis it is observed in.

currency.description: Trading currency of the close. A currency contradicting the trade rows fails the run closed.

source.description: Per-instrument source when it differs from the feed-level source.

history.description: Optional daily close series of raw observations, each as printed on its own date. Unlocks benchmark comparison, beta and alpha, the P&L curve, and account-level time-weighted return. The engine rebases a series that spans a declared split before any of those consumers difference it, so the split is not read as a market move.

splits.description: Optional split events the source shows, as [date, ratio] (a 10-for-1 split is 10). Omitted means no adjustment is applied, which is not cosmetic, on either side of the multiplication. The ledger records each trade at the share count that actually executed, so a sale after an undeclared split is subtracted from pre-split buys and a routine trim reads as a full exit (#550); and the close above is the basis its own session printed, so an undeclared split leaves a pre-split price valuing a post-split share count — a tenfold market value, weight and concentration verdict (#583). When a split falls between a close's date and the day this book is read, `consider` refuses rather than guessing which side is wrong.

fx.description: Spot rates for a mixed-currency portfolio. Omit an unavailable rate instead of guessing it. May be supplied with `prices` omitted or empty (#642) -- a rate-only envelope is a complete repair for a book refused only for a missing held-currency rate.

currency.description: Non-USD currency code; USD is fixed at 1.0 and must not be supplied.

usd_per_unit.description: USD per one unit of this currency.
